title: Activating NEDD4L suppresses EGFR-driven lung adenocarcinoma growth via facilitating EGFR proteasomal degradation.
authors: Chen, Maojian; Jiang, Wei; Zhan, Jianhua; Zhang, Shaoping; Zheng, Jiani; Huang, Yihua; He, Junyi; Yang, Yunpeng; Zhao, Shen; Zhang, Yaxiong; Liu, Jiaqing; Pang, Lanlan; Zhang, Li; Fang, Wenfeng; Li, Jing
journal: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR
one_liner_zh: 该文研究FOXM1转录因子调控NEDD4L促进EGFR降解的肿瘤机制，虽涉及TF-DNA结合（ChIP）和分子对接，但核心是湿实验与临床治疗，非TF-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法研究。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Resistant mutations and amplification of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), followed by the upregulation of its translated protein undermines the efficacy of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). This underscores that promoting EGFR protein degradation may be a promising strategy for treatment. METHODS: Ubiquitin ligases database analysis identified NEDD4L as a mediator of EGFR proteasomal degradation, which was further confirmed by qPCR, western blot, immunofluorescence staining and CO-IP. The upstream regulatory role of FOXM1 on NEDD4L was elucidated through bioinformatics analyses and validated using dual luciferase reporter assay, ChIP, qPCR, western blot and immunohistochemistry. Virtual screening and molecular docking were used to identify inhibitors of FOXM1. Functional studies and therapeutic strategies were conducted using gain- and loss-of-function assays, and evaluated through in vitro and in vivo experiments. RESULTS: We identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase NEDD4L that targets both wild-type EGFR and osimertinib-sensitive/resistant EGFR mutants for proteasomal degradation, thereby effectively inhibiting EGFR-driven LUAD growth. We found FOXM1 as a critical upstream transcription factor that binds to the promoter of NEDD4L and represses its expression, further promoting tumor growth and osimertinib resistance in LUAD by increasing EGFR protein level. High FOXM1 expression correlates with low NEDD4L expression in LUAD patients, which is associated with poor clinical outcomes. Notably, we further identified that verteporfin, an FDA-approved small molecule drug, as a FOXM1 inhibitor. Verteporfin suppresses FOXM1 to upregulate NEDD4L expression and facilitate EGFR proteasomal degradation, thereby inhibiting EGFR-driven LUAD growth and overcoming osimertinib resistance. Remarkably, the combination of verteporfin and osimertinib shows an additively inhibitory effect on EGFR-mutated LUAD growth compared to monotherapy, both in post-TKI resistance and upfront treatment settings. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that FOXM1/NEDD4L axis impairs EGFR proteasomal degradation, thus contributing to EGFR-driven LUAD growth and osimertinib resistance. Combination therapy incorporating NEDD4L activation may represent a new valued therapeutic strategy for EGFR-driven LUAD and osimertinib resistance.
abstract_zh: 背景：表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）的耐药突变和扩增，随后其翻译蛋白的上调，削弱了EGFR-酪氨酸激酶抑制剂（TKIs）在EGFR突变肺腺癌（LUAD）中的疗效。这强调促进EGFR蛋白降解可能是一种有前景的治疗策略。方法：通过泛素连接酶数据库分析，鉴定NEDD4L为EGFR蛋白酶体降解的介导因子，并通过qPCR、western blot、免疫荧光染色和CO-IP进一步确认。通过生物信息学分析阐明FOXM1对NEDD4L的上游调控作用，并使用双荧光素酶报告基因实验、ChIP、qPCR、western blot和免疫组织化学进行验证。采用虚拟筛选和分子对接 (molecular docking) 来鉴定FOXM1的抑制剂。功能研究和治疗策略通过功能获得和功能丧失实验进行，并通过体外和体内实验评估。结果：我们鉴定了E3泛素连接酶NEDD4L，它靶向野生型EGFR和奥希替尼敏感/耐药EGFR突变体进行蛋白酶体降解，从而有效抑制EGFR驱动的LUAD生长。我们发现FOXM1是一个关键的上游转录因子，它结合NEDD4L的启动子并抑制其表达，通过增加EGFR蛋白水平进一步促进LUAD肿瘤生长和奥希替尼耐药。在LUAD患者中，高FOXM1表达与低NEDD4L表达相关，这与不良临床结局相关。值得注意的是，我们进一步鉴定出verteporfin，一种FDA批准的小分子药物，作为FOXM1抑制剂。Verteporfin抑制FOXM1以上调NEDD4L表达并促进EGFR蛋白酶体降解，从而抑制EGFR驱动的LUAD生长并克服奥希替尼耐药。值得注意的是，与单药治疗相比，verteporfin和奥希替尼联合使用在TKI耐药后和初始治疗场景中均对EGFR突变LUAD生长显示出叠加抑制效果。结论：本研究证明FOXM1/NEDD4L轴损害EGFR蛋白酶体降解，从而促进EGFR驱动的LUAD生长和奥希替尼耐药。结合NEDD4L激活的联合治疗可能代表EGFR驱动LUAD和奥希替尼耐药的一种新的有价值的治疗策略。
